answer:
I ran the 3-qubit GHZ circuit on the real sirius QPU with 100 shots. The circuit was H on q0, CNOT 0 to 1, CNOT 1 to 2, then measure all. The real job is 01a15f56-0f9f-7351-a5dc-0aebafc37c5b, and it completed. Before it, I ran one free test job on sirius:mock (01a15f55-e885-756c-9ae4-716fd9f9f919) to check the circuit and the code path. The mock returned {'000': 100}.

Real counts (Qiskit bit order): 000=48, 111=34, 101=5, 011=5, 100=3, 001=3, 110=2. The fraction of shots that are 000 or 111 is 82/100 = 0.82.

Credits: the API does not report a credit amount. GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} returned metrics.billed_seconds = 1.0. Other fields were execution_seconds 0.213, runtime_seconds 0.282, and compilation.execution_runtime_estimate_seconds 1.63. The job record has no cost or credit field. The quantum-computers listing for sirius has no price field either. So I left credits_reported at 0 instead of making up a number that the API did not give. If you use the 0.3 credits per second rate from the IQM Academy calculator, which is unverified for this account, 1.0 billed second would be about 0.3 credits. The dashboard (https://resonance.iqm.tech/jobs/01a15f56-0f9f-7351-a5dc-0aebafc37c5b) shows the real billed cost.

Scripts are in the worktree: ghz_run.py and qc_list.py. The raw job JSON is in out_sirius.json.
